conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for coming in today. I’m Maya Brennan, a perinatal mental-health clinician here to support new mothers. Over the next few minutes we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. It’s a brief, 10-question form that helps us spot any symptoms of depression or anxiety that can creep up during the postpartum year. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in danger, so please answer as openly as feels safe. I’ll read each question aloud and jot your answers—no numbers or paperwork for you to wrestle with. Ready to start?

In the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? Not much at all. I can’t remember the last time I really laughed. I’ll smile if someone shows me a cute video or if my husband tries to be funny, but it feels forced—like I’m just doing it because I know I should. Mostly I’m too tired or worried to find anything truly funny right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not very often. Maybe once or twice I cracked a small smile when my husband made a dumb joke, but it felt kind of fake—like I was just going through the motions. Most of the time I’m too worn-out or on-edge to feel any real laughter.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk, even a shower without interruption—but now it all feels like one more chore. I’ll think “I should enjoy this,” but the feeling just isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, my brain immediately says it’s because I’m not doing something right—maybe my milk isn’t good enough or I missed his sleepy cue. I’ll replay every little thing and find a way it’s my fault. I know it’s probably unreasonable, but I can’t stop the guilty thoughts from showing up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty often. I’ll be sitting there and suddenly feel like something awful is about to happen—like the baby isn’t breathing or I left the stove on. I check him constantly, even when he’s sleeping peacefully. I know I’m being irrational, but the worry just grabs me and won’t let go.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… sometimes it hits me out of nowhere. My heart starts racing and I feel like I can’t catch my breath, even when everything looks fine on the outside. I’ll be rocking the baby in the quiet nursery and suddenly feel this wave of dread, like something terrible is about to happen. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

A lot of the time. It feels like there’s this endless list—feed the baby, change him, try to sleep, wash bottles, pump—and if one thing goes off schedule I feel like the whole day collapses. Sometimes I just sit on the couch staring at the mess, thinking I’ll never dig myself out. I manage the basics, but it’s like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… most nights I lie there even when the baby’s finally down. My mind keeps spinning—did I burp him long enough, why didn’t he finish that last feed, what if he wakes up screaming again. By the time I doze off it’s usually almost morning, and then I start worrying I won’t hear him if he cries. I probably get three broken hours, if that.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I feel that way most days. It’s like this heavy cloud that just sits on me. I’ll look at the baby sleeping and instead of feeling happy, I feel guilty for not enjoying him more. Some mornings I wake up already discouraged, before anything’s even happened.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A few times this week. Usually it’s when I’m alone—like when I’m trying to get him to nap and he keeps fighting it, or when I drop a bottle and spill pumped milk everywhere. I’ll just sit on the nursery floor and cry because it feels like I can’t do even the smallest thing right.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel overwhelmed and sad, but I’ve never wanted to hurt myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Patient: 3–4 wks post-delivery, first-time mother, partner support present.

Responses to Edinburgh-type 10-item questionnaire indicate:

Symptoms/behaviors endorsed:
- Depressed mood daily, crying spells 3× this week (Q8, Q9)
- Marked anhedonia: no real laughter, no anticipation of pleasure (Q1, Q2)
- Excessive self-blame/guilt re parenting competence (Q3)
- Persistent, intrusive, generalized anxiety and panic symptoms without clear trigger (Q4, Q5)
- Subjective overwhelm, feels “treading water,” tasks piling up (Q6)
- Mood-related insomnia: difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep even when infant settled (Q7)

Patterns:
- Symptoms present "most days," interfere with functioning and attachment experience
- No current thoughts of self-harm or harm to infant (Q10)

Risk factors highlighted:
- Moderate-severe depressive features (low mood, anhedonia, guilt)
- Comorbid anxiety/panic
- Sleep deprivation secondary to rumination
- Absence of suicidal ideation → no immediate safety concern per self-report

Screening impression:
Findings exceed "baby blues" threshold; meet provisional probable range for postpartum major depressive episode with anxious features. Recommend formal diagnostic evaluation and discussion of treatment/support options at earliest convenience.
